subject: Request: custom SLA exhibit + order form language for enterprise MSA/SOW
messages:
From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@mediwave.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@mediwave.com, legal@mediwave.com
Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA exhibit deviation + order form language for MSA/SOW

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profiles looked promising. Procurement and legal asked me to follow up formally with the customer-side SLA asks so we can get an exhibit attached to our MSA/SOW and confirm the order form language for DocuSign. Attached are our internal ask doc and the procurement intake form. High-level asks: 

- Availability: Target 99.95% monthly availability for the hosted inference endpoint used by our production tenant.
- Latency: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 250ms for single-request online inference (typical 512-token prompts).
- Exception carveouts: Allowed maintenance windows (2x2hr per quarter), regional failover events, and documented capacity exhaustion if usage exceeds committed capacity in the order form.
- Credits: Tiered credits for monthly availability deficits (we included a proposed schedule in the attachment).
- Evidence: We require quarterly telemetry exports (masked), a short runbook for incident response, and a contact list for escalation.

Our procurement timeline is tight — we need final order form language and the exhibit redlines within two business weeks to hit our board approval window.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept 99.95 with the carveouts above and, if so, share a draft exhibit/order form language we can route to our legal? If any of the latency SLOs are infeasible for the managed SKU we discussed, please indicate the alternative you recommend (e.g., Dedicated or pinned capacity).

Appreciate it —
Alicia Torres
Head of Procurement
MediWave Health

Attachments: MediWave_SLA_Request.pdf (3 pages), MediWave_Procurement_Form.xlsx (1 sheet)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@mediwave.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exhibit deviation + order form language for MSA/SOW

Alicia — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Confirming receipt and timeline: we can prioritize a draft exhibit and order form language and get back within 5 business days with a baseline redline and technical notes. Quick answers up-front:

- Availability 99.95%: We can propose 99.95% monthly for Hosted with two important caveats we will document in the exhibit (regional outage carveouts, and capacity-exhaustion carveouts tied to the committed capacity line in the order form).
- Latency p99 250ms: For shared hosted pools this is aggressive at sustained peak; p50/p95 targets look achievable for typical prompt sizes. If you need deterministic p99 at that latency for all traffic patterns, we should evaluate: a) Dedicated capacity, or b) a pinned-node deployment.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal technical review (Karthik) to call out precise wording we need around "capacity-exhaustion" and telemetry exports.
2) Sales/legal (Marissa) to draft order form committed capacity lines and credit schedule.
3) I'll send a redwood_custom_sla_template_v1.pdf as a starting exhibit for your legal to review.

I'll attach the template and loop back with a redline by EOD Tuesday. If procurement can share committed QPS or monthly token volume, Karthik can map that to a recommendation (Hosted vs Dedicated).

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: SLA exhibit deviation + order form language for MSA/SOW

Hi all — looping in technical details from the infra side. Short version: we can support the availability target with the carveouts Alicia proposed, but we need precise order form language around "committed capacity" and operational controls. A few specific asks/notes: 

1) Committed capacity definition: please confirm whether "committed capacity" will be described as a sustained token/sec metric, a concurrent request target, or a monthly token volume with burst allowances. Our credit schedule must map to whichever metric you commit to.

2) Capacity-exhaustion carveout wording (suggested): 
   - "Availability failures resulting from Customer exceeding committed capacity as defined in the Order Form, or resulting from Customer traffic patterns that exceed the deployment’s trained performance profile, shall be excluded from Availability calculations provided Redwood made commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate including notification and recommended mitigation steps."

3) Telemetry & evidence: we can provide quarterly masked telemetry exports and a 1-page incident runbook. For audit-grade evidence (SOC2-style), we recommend the Dedicated SKU and an agreed evidence delivery SLA.

4) Latency SLOs: p50/p95 are fine for Hosted. p99 <=250ms for all traffic is only realistic on Dedicated or pinned instances for the committed QPS you listed. If MediWave expects to operate at high concurrency, let's map traffic via the procurement form to a recommended pool size.

I'll prepare suggested redlines for the order form's committed capacity and the carveout text by EOD Monday and attach to the template Rishi provided.

-Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 16:21:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: SLA exhibit deviation + order form language for MSA/SOW

Alicia — thanks for your patience. We've reviewed internally and attached a lightly redlined exhibit and proposed order form language (see redwood_custom_sla_template_v1.pdf). Summary of what Redwood can sign today: 

- Availability commitment: 99.95% monthly for the Hosted inference endpoint with the following explicit carveouts: scheduled maintenance (2x2hr/quarter with 7-day notice), regional provider outage beyond Redwood control, and customer-exceeded committed capacity (as defined in the order form).
- Credits: tiered monthly credits tied to % monthly availability shortfalls (we included a three-band schedule in the template).
- Latency: p50/p95 commitments for Hosted are included; p99 commitment of <=250ms is only available on Dedicated. We included sample language to add a Dedicated line item to the order form if you choose that path.
- Evidence: quarterly masked telemetry export + 1-page incident runbook. For additional audit evidence we recommend Dedicated + an evidence add-on.

Action items: 
1) Please confirm the committed capacity metric you'd prefer (token/sec or monthly tokens + burst) — once you confirm we'll lock the order form numbers.
2) If legal prefers different carveout phrasing, send redlines; otherwise we'll publish the exhibit and route a DocuSign envelope for the order form + exhibit next week.

DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/RW-MW-SLA-0317 (preview only; final envelope will be sent after capacity metric confirmation).

If you want a quick call to resolve the capacity metric, Rishi and Karthik are available this week.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
